comment: The data of crypto's generated tables and of llms.txt; doc/tables/generate.py reads it with the test Jamfiles, the message tests and the superproject's Jamfile fixtures, and writes doc/generated/, doc/llms.txt, include/webcpp/crypto/detail/capabilities.hpp and test/capabilities_test.cpp. The capability table is `families`: per family its algorithms, the targets on which each backend has it (each claimed only where a test of the family's operations on that backend runs), constant time per target where it differs from the backend's own `constant_time` (none yet), and the default per target and what the program links, as the code has it now, with its reason and the tests that fix it; a backend with `targets`, where it is built, is a tag of `backends`. A name in a text is written between backticks, as Markdown writes code: the tables show it as code and llms.txt keeps the backticks. Edit this file, then run python3 libs/crypto/doc/tables/generate.py; the doc build runs it with --check.

bearssl.title: BearSSL
bearssl.library: BearSSL, commit 7bea48e5 of the mirror webcpporg/bearssl, built from source
bearssl.allocation: none: the key schedule and GCM's state live inside the object
bearssl.constant_time: by design: `aes_ct64` and `ghash_ctmul64`, or AES-NI and PCLMUL where the CPU has them; on a 32-bit host a 64-bit multiplication may not be constant time, which BearSSL documents

openssl.title: OpenSSL
openssl.library: OpenSSL 3.5.9's libcrypto, built from source and static
openssl.allocation: `make` allocates the cipher's context through OpenSSL's own allocator, outside the program's resource, unless a native program sets `WEBCPP_CRYPTO_OPENSSL_MEMORY_RESOURCE`, which sends every allocation of OpenSSL's in the process to `openssl_memory_resource()`; a message allocates nothing after `make`
openssl.constant_time: with assembly (native Clang and GCC), AES-NI and carry-less multiplication where the CPU has them; built no-asm (MSVC, wasip2, wasip3), table-based AES and 4-bit GHASH, neither constant time (`OPENSSL_AES_CONST_TIME` makes only the AES core constant time; GHASH stays table-based)

ctaes.title: ctaes
ctaes.library: ctaes as Bitcoin Core v31.1 ships it (`src/crypto/ctaes`), built from source
ctaes.own_api: `<ctaes.h>`: `AES128_init`, `AES128_encrypt` and `AES128_decrypt`, the same for 192 and 256, on whole blocks
ctaes.allocation: none: the key schedule lives inside the object
ctaes.constant_time: by design: bitsliced, no table and no branch on secret data

secp256k1.title: libsecp256k1
secp256k1.library: libsecp256k1 v0.8.0, built from source with every module on
secp256k1.allocation: `keypair::make` allocates the signing context, once, in the `std::pmr::memory_resource` it is given; nothing else allocates
secp256k1.constant_time: by design: signing and key generation are constant time and constant memory access

system.title: the system's generator
system.library: getentropy on Linux, macOS and WASI; BCryptGenRandom on Windows; crypto.getRandomValues through Emscripten
system.constant_time: not applicable: it reads the system's generator

none.title: no backend
none.constant_time: `equal` is constant time in the contents: every byte is read, no branch and no index depends on one

operations.what: Unpredictable bytes from the operating system's or the browser's generator, and nothing else.
Compares two tags or MACs in constant time.
Every failure's value, fixed and never reused, in the category webcpp.crypto.
The AES block cipher on whole 16-byte blocks: a building block, not encryption of data.
operations.default: `aes256<>` names the default backend; where that is BearSSL, its `make` does not compile, and the program names `aes256<backends::ctaes>`.

operations.what: AES-GCM, authenticated encryption in place with an incremental seal.
A secp256k1 key pair: BIP 340 Schnorr and ECDSA signatures, ECDH and the x-only tweak.
Verifies a BIP 340 or an ECDSA signature with a public key alone.
ECDSA's strict DER encoding and its low-S form.
Tweaks an x-only public key by a 32-byte tweak a protocol computes.
With `WEBCPP_CRYPTO_OPENSSL_MEMORY_RESOURCE`, natively, every allocation of OpenSSL's in the process goes to a `std::pmr::memory_resource` the program defines.

default.why: the only AEAD backend there: webcpp does not build OpenSSL for Emscripten; size and speed not measured yet
constant time by design ({bearssl-ct}), where OpenSSL is built no-asm and its AES and GHASH are table-based ({openssl-install})

OpenSSL's assembly uses the CPU's AES and carry-less multiplication instructions on x86-64 and ARMv8 ({openssl-armv8}; {openssl-ghash-asm}); BearSSL has them on x86 only ({bearssl-aes}); speed not measured yet

the same rule as with Clang and GCC, but here OpenSSL is built no-asm: table-based AES and 4-bit GHASH, no AES-NI, not constant time ({openssl-install}); where timing attacks matter, link BearSSL and define `WEBCPP_CRYPTO_DEFAULT_BACKEND_BEARSSL`
the program's choice, constant time by design ({bearssl-ct}): on MSVC, where OpenSSL is built no-asm, the choice for code that timing attacks threaten
a raw block cipher is a building block a program chooses deliberately, naming its backend; `aes256<>` takes AES-GCM's default as its argument, and its `make` does not compile where that is BearSSL

rules.title: Never reuse an IV under one key
rules.text: two AES-GCM messages under one key and one IV reveal the XOR of their plaintexts and let an attacker forge tags for every later message ({joux}; {nonce-reuse}); draw a random 12-byte IV per message, or use a counter that never repeats, a restart included.

rules.title: The usage limit
rules.text: with random IVs, at most 2^32 messages under one key ({sp800-38d}, section 8.3); rotate the key before.

rules.title: A failed open zeroes data
rules.text: when the tag does not match, `open` returns `authentication_failed` and zeroes the whole of `data`; keep a copy of the ciphertext if it is needed after a failure. There is no incremental open: a large message is split into records.

rules.title: Records: each stream its own key
rules.text: records numbered from 0 with the number as IV are safe only under a key used for that one stream: derive a key per stream (HKDF of the storage key with a random salt) or draw one; never number two streams' records under one key.

rules.title: ECDH's form
rules.text: `keypair::ecdh` returns libsecp256k1's hashed form, the SHA-256 of the compressed shared point; it does not interoperate with protocols that take the raw x coordinate, such as Nostr's NIP-44 ({nip44}). Derive keys from it with HKDF, never use it directly.

rules.title: The x-only tweak is not BIP 32
rules.text: `tweak_xonly` is BIP 341's even-y arithmetic ({bip341}); BIP 32's child derivation needs a tweak of the full key, which this version does not offer ({bip32}).

rules.title: Ethereum
rules.text: this version verifies Ethereum's ECDSA signatures with a known key but has no recoverable signature (no recovery id `v`, no public key recovery) and no uncompressed public key output, so it cannot sign Ethereum transactions or derive addresses.

rules.title: Compare secrets in constant time
rules.text: compare a tag, a MAC or a token with `equal`, never `==` or `memcmp` ({cwe208}).

rules.title: Secrets come from random_device
rules.text: keys, IVs and tokens are drawn from `random_device`, never `std::mt19937` or `rand` ({cwe338}).

rules.title: The default on MSVC is not constant time
rules.text: natively with OpenSSL linked the default is OpenSSL, which MSVC builds no-asm, table-based ({openssl-install}); where timing attacks matter, link BearSSL and define `WEBCPP_CRYPTO_DEFAULT_BACKEND_BEARSSL`.

elsewhere.memory: `config.hpp` refuses the option on every WebAssembly target

root.title: webcpp::crypto
rows: Keys, IVs, tokens, nonces: every secret a program draws
you need a random number an attacker must not predict; never `std::mt19937` or `rand` ({cwe338})
Checking a tag, a MAC or a token
you compare anything secret; never `==` or `memcmp` on a MAC
you branch on a failure: forged data, a wrong size, no entropy
Keeping every allocation of OpenSSL's in the program's own resource, natively
a native program on OpenSSL must allocate only from its own arena; on WebAssembly, BearSSL allocates nothing

ciphers.title: webcpp::crypto::ciphers
columns: Speed, with and without hardware support
rows: not resistant: a repeated IV under one key reveals the plaintexts' XOR and lets tags be forged ({joux}, {nonce-reuse})
BearSSL and OpenSSL with assembly: yes; OpenSSL no-asm (MSVC, wasip2, wasip3): no
TLS 1.3 ({rfc8446}), SSH ({rfc5647}), IPsec ({rfc4106}), SRTP ({rfc7714}), optional for WebRTC's media ({rfc8827})
you encrypt a message, a record or a file: secrecy and integrity together
not applicable: equal blocks give equal ciphertext
ctaes: yes; OpenSSL with assembly: yes; OpenSSL no-asm: no
you need one keyed permutation of a 16-byte block, such as an opaque identifier; for data, use AES-GCM

curves.title: webcpp::crypto::curves
rows: BIP 340 Schnorr and ECDSA signatures, ECDH, the x-only tweak
secret 32 bytes; public 33 bytes compressed, 32 bytes x-only
64 bytes; ECDSA in DER up to 72
no: WebCrypto offers P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519 and X25519, not secp256k1 ({webcrypto})

Bitcoin's keys and signatures; Nostr's event signatures ({nip01}); Ethereum's ECDSA verification with a known key. Not in this version: Ethereum's recoverable signatures and its addresses from the uncompressed key; ECDH in the raw x-coordinate form of Nostr's encrypted messages ({nip44}); BIP 32's derivation ({bip32})

fixes.no_backend_native: Add `/webcpp/crypto//openssl` or `/third_party//bearssl` to the program's sources.
fixes.bearssl_not_linked: Add `/third_party//bearssl`, or, with OpenSSL linked, define `WEBCPP_CRYPTO_DEFAULT_BACKEND_OPENSSL`.
fixes.openssl_only_on_wasi: On WASI the default is BearSSL: add `/third_party//bearssl`, or define `WEBCPP_CRYPTO_DEFAULT_BACKEND_OPENSSL`.
fixes.openssl_old: Name `/webcpp/crypto//openssl`, which builds OpenSSL 3.5.9; without b2, put OpenSSL 3's `include/` first.
fixes.canary_sodium_other_commit: Build the library at the commit of webcpp's submodule, or link it through b2.
fixes.gcm_on_ctaes: Use `aes256_gcm` with BearSSL or OpenSSL linked.
fixes.secp256k1_other_backend: Name `backends::secp256k1`, or leave the backend out: `curves::secp256k1::keypair`.
fixes.two_defaults: Keep one of the two defines.
fixes.default_openssl_on_emscripten: Remove the define, or make it `WEBCPP_CRYPTO_DEFAULT_BACKEND_BEARSSL`.
fixes.openssl_on_emscripten: Name `/third_party//bearssl` in its place for the Emscripten build.
fixes.openssl_memory_on_emscripten: Remove `<define>WEBCPP_CRYPTO_OPENSSL_MEMORY_RESOURCE` from the WebAssembly build: give that build a project of its own, without the define and OpenSSL, naming `/third_party//bearssl`. On WebAssembly the backend is BearSSL, which allocates nothing.
fixes.openssl_memory_on_webassembly: Remove `<define>WEBCPP_CRYPTO_OPENSSL_MEMORY_RESOURCE` from the WebAssembly build: give that build a project of its own, without the define and OpenSSL, naming `/third_party//bearssl`. On WebAssembly the backend is BearSSL, which allocates nothing.
fixes.memory_missing_definition_install: Define `std::pmr::memory_resource& webcpp::crypto::openssl_memory_resource() noexcept` once in the program, returning a resource that is never destroyed.
fixes.memory_missing_definition_make: Define `std::pmr::memory_resource& webcpp::crypto::openssl_memory_resource() noexcept` once in the program, returning a resource that is never destroyed.
fixes.memory_two_files: Give the define in the requirements of the program's project, with OpenSSL beside it, `project app : requirements <define>WEBCPP_CRYPTO_OPENSSL_MEMORY_RESOURCE <library>/webcpp/crypto//openssl ;`, so that every target of the program gets both.
fixes.openssl_memory_not_linked: A target has the define and not OpenSSL: put `<library>/webcpp/crypto//openssl` in the same project requirements as the define, or remove the define.
fixes.canary_missing: Link the library through b2, `/third_party//bearssl`; built by other means, it must be the pinned commit, with webcpp's `src/canary_bearssl.c`.
fixes.canary_other_commit: Build the library at the commit of webcpp's submodule, or link it through b2.
fixes.canary_other_configuration: Build BearSSL in webcpp's configuration (`getentropy`), or link it through b2.
fixes.canary_without: Compile webcpp's `src/canary_bearssl.c` with the library, or link it through b2.
fixes.canary_secp256k1_small: Give the program and the library the same `<webcpp-secp256k1-tables>`, or link through b2.
fixes.canary_secp256k1_two_files: Compile every file of the program with the same backend settings.
fixes.canary_two_files: Compile every file of the program with the same backend settings.
fixes.default_two_files: Give `WEBCPP_CRYPTO_DEFAULT_BACKEND_*` in the requirements of the program's project, so that every file gets it.
